presentation.label: OVERVIEW
presentation.title: DAGESTAN
presentation.p1: A republic of the Russian Caucasus between mountains and the Caspian Sea, Dagestan produces more wrestling champions per capita than anywhere in the world. Here, wrestling is not a sport: it is a social fact. Every village has its champions, tournaments are fought between valleys, and boys start wrestling before they learn to read.
presentation.p2: Makhachkala and its region line up dozens of gyms where hundreds of international-level athletes train daily, many of whom later move into world MMA. These gyms do not open to passing visitors: you get in by invitation. That is exactly the access MKR opens for you.

safety.p1: No empty phrases: Western governments, including the UK FCDO, advise against travel to Dagestan. That is the official frame and you should know it. The ground reality our athletes live is different: Makhachkala and Kaspiysk are active, stable cities, used to foreign athletes, where hospitality towards fighters is a local pride.
safety.p2: Between the two, MKR does not leave you to figure it out alone: local liaisons with you at all times, organised transport, urban areas only, full pre-departure briefing, 24/7 emergency contact and mandatory repatriation insurance. You leave informed, supported, never alone.
safety.testimonial_quote: I went alone, without speaking Russian. The welcome is incredible. On the mat, the level is brutal.

items.question: Is Dagestan safe for a foreign athlete in 2026?
items.answer: Official frame first: the UK FCDO advises against all travel to Dagestan, and most Western governments advise against travel to Russia. Ground reality next: the training cities (Makhachkala, Kaspiysk) are stable and host foreign athletes all year round, and hospitality towards athletes is a local pride. MKR manages the whole stay: permanent local liaisons, urban areas only, pre-departure briefing, 24/7 emergency contact, mandatory repatriation insurance.

items.question: Why does Dagestan produce so many wrestling champions?
items.answer: Three measurable reasons. Culture: wrestling starts at age 5, every village has its gym, and a serious wrestler logs around 5,000 hours of mat time before turning 18. Volume: more than 50,000 registered wrestlers around Makhachkala compete for places. Selection: only the best emerge from permanent competition. The result: 30+ Olympic medals for the region, including 8 titles for the city of Khasavyurt alone over the last 4 cycles.

items.question: How do you get to Dagestan from Europe?
items.answer: There is no direct flight from Western Europe. The route goes through Istanbul: you book a flight to Istanbul (your side), then the Istanbul-Makhachkala (MCX) domestic flight, included in your MKR package, about 2h30 in the air. On arrival, an MKR liaison meets you at the airport and the 1h30 transfer to camp is included.

items.question: Can you train in local gyms without an invitation?
items.answer: No, and that is the point everyone underestimates when trying to organise the trip alone. Dagestani gyms work by co-optation: you must be introduced by a coach or a trusted member of the network. Without an invitation, you stay at the door. MKR access is built on the personal network of Ruslan Mukhtarov, born in Dagestan and a former member of the French Olympic wrestling team.

items.question: Can you pay by card on site?
items.answer: No. Visa and Mastercard cards issued outside Russia work neither in shops nor at ATMs. Bring cash in euros to exchange for rubles on site (our liaisons take you to the exchange office). Since your MKR package covers housing, meals and transport, pocket money stays limited: plan the equivalent of 50 to 100 euros per week for extras.

items.question: When is the best time for a camp in Dagestan?
items.answer: April to September for the most pleasant climate, but the gyms run all year. MKR organises 4 official sessions per year (summer, autumn, winter, spring). With capacity capped at 15 spots per discipline, the real constraint is availability more than weather.

presentation.label: OVERVIEW
presentation.title: CHECHNYA
presentation.p1: A republic of the Russian Caucasus west of Dagestan, Chechnya has become the epicentre of modern MMA in fifteen years. Grozny hosts state structures and private teams that pay their fighters a monthly salary, and the world's 2nd largest MMA organisation by ranked fighters holds its events there.
presentation.p2: Akhmat Fight Club and the professional gyms of Grozny concentrate a level of sparring you will not find anywhere in Europe. This is the ecosystem MKR opens for its MMA camps, with liaisons on site and direct partnerships with the gyms.

safety.p1: No empty phrases: the UK FCDO specifically advises against travel to Chechnya, and most Western governments advise against travel to Russia. That is the official frame and you should know it. The ground reality: Grozny today is an orderly, tightly controlled city with low street crime, where foreign athletes are welcomed with respect.
safety.p2: Between the two, MKR runs a full protocol: permanent local liaisons, accredited partner gyms, urban areas only, detailed pre-departure briefing, 24/7 emergency contact and mandatory repatriation insurance. Local culture is Muslim and conservative: modest dress, no alcohol, respect for local customs. Everything is covered in the briefing.

items.answer: Official frame first: the UK FCDO specifically advises against travel to Chechnya, and most Western governments advise against travel to Russia. MKR manages the entire stay: permanent local liaisons, partner gyms, pre-departure briefing, 24/7 emergency contact and mandatory repatriation insurance.

items.question: Why did Grozny become an epicentre of world MMA?
items.answer: Because the region industrialised fighter development: state and private teams pay their fighters monthly, professional gyms number in the dozens, and the world's 2nd largest MMA organisation by ranked fighters holds its events there. Add the Caucasian wrestling heritage as the technical base, and you get a density of high-level sparring partners that does not exist in Europe.

items.question: How do you get to Grozny from Europe?
items.answer: No direct flight from Western Europe. The route goes through Istanbul: flight to Istanbul on your side, then the direct Istanbul-Grozny (GRV) domestic flight, about 2h30, included in your MKR package. A liaison meets you at the airport and the transfer to camp takes only 30 minutes, also included.

items.question: What level do you need to train MMA in Grozny?
items.answer: Advanced level is required: 5+ years of regular practice or competition experience. The application form blocks lower levels, and Ruslan confirms your level on the video call. This is not elitism: your sparring partners are professionals, and the pace of the sessions assumes a real technical base. If you are not there yet, the Wrestling camp in Dagestan is the best way in.

items.question: Can you visit Chechnya during the camp?
items.answer: Yes, on rest day. Optional excursions include the Heart of Chechnya Mosque in Grozny, the medieval Vainakh towers of Itum-Kale and the high-altitude lake Kezenoy-Am. Always accompanied by MKR liaisons: the mountain areas are not for solo visits.
